truth.problem: exportProviderCatalogSnapshot wraps writeOwnerOnlyFileAtomic in an empty `catch (e) {}` and then unconditionally returns { ok: true, path }.
truth.impact: When the destination is unwritable (missing dir, permission denied, disk full) the export reports success with a path that holds no snapshot; syncPinnedSnapshot(dir, true) and any caller tell the operator the catalog is pinned when it is not, and the later offline fallback silently finds nothing.

truth.problem: The JSON.parse catch writes a message to stderr and then rethrows the same error.
truth.impact: Callers that also report the thrown error print the failure a second time; the function should either log-and-handle or wrap-and-throw, not both.

decoys.problem: removeProviderCatalogEntry swallows every lock/write error in a catch that holds only a comment.
decoys.impact: A prune that fails leaves the entry in the cache without telling the caller.
decoys.quote: // Best-effort, like every other write in this module.
decoys.why_not_a_defect: This is the module's consistent, documented posture: every cache writer (saveProviderCatalogCache, clearProviderCatalogCache, updateProviderCatalogEntry) is best-effort because the cache is a courtesy. The JSDoc states the reason and it holds: the next full refresh writes only the providers it looked at, so an undropped entry is not carried over and ages out. The import result does not claim pruning happened, so no caller is misled.

candidate.problem: exportProviderCatalogSnapshot swallows a failed snapshot write with an empty, uncommented catch, then returns `{ ok: true, path: destPath, summary }`. `ok` is hard-coded true, so it cannot report the failure at all. This breaks error-handling.mdc Rule 3 and Iron Law 1. The docstring says the function exists so that a caller never wrongly believes it has a snapshot, but that is exactly what happens here.
candidate.impact: Trigger: the destination is not writable (read-only config dir, disk full, a missing parent dir under an air-gapped CI layout). Outcome: syncPinnedSnapshot(dir, true), called from loadOrRefreshWith in provider-catalog.ts:270, returns a summary that reads as success. No pinned file exists, so the offline fallback this feature is for silently never works. Any future CLI caller printing `result.ok`/`result.path` would tell the operator a snapshot was written when none was.

candidate.problem: The pin side-path can throw out of loadOrRefreshWith, which is the module's best-effort cache policy (every other cache write here swallows its failures). exportProviderCatalogSnapshot throws when the cache is absent. That happens right after saveProviderCatalogCache, which itself silently gives up on a 250 ms lock timeout. importProviderCatalogSnapshot throws on a corrupt or wrong-version pinned file (snapshot.ts:89-109). Neither call is guarded.
candidate.impact: Trigger: lock contention makes saveProviderCatalogCache drop the write (line 270), or a hand-edited or old-version pinned file is present when a refresh comes back empty (line 274). Outcome: the provider catalog load rejects. In the first case a valid `fresh` catalog is thrown away, and in the second the caller gets an exception instead of the empty catalog it got before. So the courtesy pin feature can break the /routing picker and `providers status`.

candidate.problem: The import docstring describes merge behaviour that has no code path: "An entry already in the cache that is newer than the snapshot's copy is kept; only older or missing entries are replaced." The loop at line 129 calls updateProviderCatalogEntry unconditionally, and that call overwrites `[entry.name]` with no fetchedAt comparison (provider-catalog-cache.ts:234).
candidate.impact: The next reader or caller relies on the doc and expects a stale pinned snapshot not to clobber fresher live entries. It does, so the docstring misleads whoever maintains or calls the import.
candidate.quote:

candidate.problem: The JSON parse catch logs to stderr and rethrows the same raw SyntaxError. Every sibling failure in the function instead throws a contextual `provider catalog snapshot: ...` Error. This breaks error-handling.mdc Rule 5: log and rethrow in one catch, with no contextual wrapper and `cause` on the rethrow.
candidate.impact: Callers that report the error print the message twice (stderr line plus the caller's own report), and the thrown error does not say which file or operation failed. A library function writing directly to process.stderr also pollutes TUI output.
